verdicts.reason: ARLEN/ARBURST are driven by the bridge (AXI master); RLAST is driven by the slave response. Checkable on the AXI interface every cycle. Actor must be master (bridge) for the request side.
The bridge, acting as AXI master, issues the writes. Actor should be master. Checkable via AWLEN/AWBURST.
The bridge generates the AXI IDs, so actor is master. ID rotation after completed transactions is a multi-transaction sequence, best exercised in a scenario. Count is configuration-dependent.
The bridge must not have more than one outstanding transaction per direction, so actor is master. Checkable from handshake counters.
Describes unbounded response latency tolerance. There is no checkable pass/fail criterion as 'indefinitely' can't be verified, and actor is not the slave.
Rule is supported by the quote: AHB slave side of the bridge returns ERROR and issues no AXI request. Fields are acceptable but the quote is truncated; the strength is MUST. Keep as is.
The mapping is stated by the quote, but the bridge drives AxPROT on AXI as master. Strength and check are fine.
The mapping is stated, but the bridge drives AxCACHE on AXI as master. Check by assertion is OK.
The quote states one AXI single per transfer and waiting for BRESP. Actor is the bridge as AXI master.
The quote states single-beat writes without aggregation; the bridge issues the AXI writes, so actor is master.
MAY aggregation is stated for eligible Write-back bufferable fixed bursts with constant attributes. The scenario check is appropriate.
The quote states a single accepted address gives one R beat, with no speculative or multi-beat reads. The bridge as AXI master issues the read.
The quote states one AHB beat maps to one AXI single and waits for BRESP. The bridge issues the writes, so actor is master.
The quote supports the rule. The bridge issues the AXI burst, so actor is master. The scenario check is correct.
The quote states no AXI request for the rejected transfer, a two-cycle AHB ERROR, and draining the accepted write prefix. The AHB slave side is the actor.
Non-OKAY AXI response maps to AHB ERROR as stated by the quote. The AHB-slave side of the bridge is the actor.

duplicates.reason: Both state that writes are single-beat with no aggregation. AA-T1.7.3.4-02 is the clearer statement, including the BRESP wait.

questions.question: Does the AXI ID count apply per direction and how is it configured? Rotation after each completed transaction conflicts with 'count > 1 does not enable concurrency'. Is the ID checked at each address handshake or at response?

The Write-back bufferable-burst aggregation is optional (MAY) in one place and described as a full-burst MUST in another. Which behavior applies, and what is the intended response for an incomplete burst?
Writes are said to be single-beat in one rule but bursts of up to 16 beats are allowed in another. Which memory types permit bursts?
How long is the AHB wait allowed to be when no R/B response arrives? Is there a timeout?
